description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2429-2431 — when updating nc_constrained_types during NC state update, only entries from new_permitted are ORed in:
  `for entry in new_permitted.iter() { nc_constrained_types |= name_type_bit(&entry.base); }`

This is correct for each CA that asserts a permittedSubtrees constraint. Each CA contributes its own types. The invariant says bits are only ORed in — once constrained, always constrained. This is the correct RFC 5280 §6.1.4(b) behavior.

However there is a subtle issue in the intersection logic at lines 2457-2505: when computing the intersection of current and new_permitted, if a type appears in new_permitted but NOT in current, the code adds it directly (line 2465-2466: 'Type not previously constrained → add directly'). This is correct — a new CA is adding a constraint for a type not previously constrained.

But the code also adds entries from current when same_type_in_new is empty (line 2484-2486: 'Type not in new_permitted → keep unchanged'). This is also correct — new_permitted doesn't constrain that type, so current's constraint is preserved.

The intersection is correct. Not a real bug.
title: NC permitted intersection: type-tracking bits set only from new_permitted, not current
